slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
A radian is the central angle that intercepts an arc as long as the radius. Its measure is arc length divided by radius, θ = s/r.

The whole circle's arc is 2πr, so a full turn is 2π radians: 360 degrees = 2π radians, and 180 degrees = π radians. One radian is about 57.3 degrees.

Enrichment: radians are not in the 2023 Indiana Geometry standards; they preview Algebra II and precalculus.
